doc.title: Albert Warner and Sonny Henry Interview, 1959-01-08

title: Parade formation and the Eureka's drums placement
summary: They compare old and current order of trombones, tuba, baritone, altos, trumpets and drums in a parade band.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: name. Well, we'll ask him. He'll know. Yeah. I can't think of his dad. I just want to get those guys. I can't think of his dad's name. I was going to ask about, in marching, the trombones are always out in front, but where does the tuba belong? Right with you or sometimes the tuba in back of you in the old days? Way back. Two supporters always be in the front. No, no, but some time ago the tuba used to be behind us because if you had two trombones, the tuba used to be back to the second. But now here up late, we got to show that we go three. Three in the front. But if you had only two in a row and two trombones, and then the tuba in back. Who else back there with him? Well, on this side, on that side, that's your tuba and your... Sacks? Yeah. Where'd the baritone horn go? Out through, Sacks, and in the back, behind me. Baritone horn back of you? Yeah, behind me, yeah. Over on the right side? Yeah, behind Al, yeah. With the tuba? Yeah. Oh, yeah, you mean with the old big baritone. That's right, with the tuba, that's right. Yeah, baritone. That's right. Where'd the alto horns come? Yeah, he'd come next. Next. Where was the clarinet? Were they... They'd come next to the trumpet, but the trumpet would be last. The trumpets last or the drums last? No, no, no. Yes, no, no. The trumpet would be next to the alto and then the drums. And the drums in the rail. The drums last. The drums last. How come the Eureka does it the other way now? They put the trumpets in back?

Well, yeah. I don't know if that... I don't know how Poisey's got that lined up now, but I noticed that myself. He put the drums in the... In the middle of it. In between... Between Paul and then, yeah. I noticed that myself.
In the old days, I understand the drums always in back.
Always in the back. Right, right.
I wonder if he had a reason for that, or...? I don't know.
Well, he didn't say what was his reason or anything. I don't know.
I imagine he likes to stay back there where he can keep an eye on the whole band. Yeah, no, I guess... That might be it.
He's going towards them all. Keep an eye on that time, you know? Yeah. So in case they get out of that time, well, then he could call them down.
That's the only band that does it that way that I ever saw. I wonder why you did it to them.

Yeah. That might be the reason. That's his reason. Yeah, you have to be, yeah. That might be his reason. You see, to keep the... When those drums get out of line, that he could be right there to guard them, you know? Get them in right.
